text: Christ set us free for freedom itself. So stand your ground, and don't get tangled up again in a yoke of slavery.
Listen closely — I, Paul, tell you: if you get circumcised, Christ will do you no good at all.
I'll say it again to everyone who accepts circumcision: you're now obligated to keep the entire law.
You who are trying to be made right with God through the law have cut yourselves off from Christ; you've fallen out of grace.
But through the Spirit, by faith, we're eagerly waiting for the righteousness we hope for.
In Christ Jesus, neither circumcision nor its absence counts for anything — only faith working through love matters.
You were running so well. Who cut in and kept you from obeying the truth?
That kind of persuasion doesn't come from the one who calls you.
A little yeast works through the whole batch of dough.
I'm confident in the Lord that you won't take a different view; whoever is confusing you will bear the judgment, whoever they are.
As for me, brothers, if I still preached circumcision, why am I still being persecuted? If I did, the cross would no longer be an offense.
I wish those stirring you up would go all the way and cut themselves off completely.
You, brothers, were called to freedom — just don't use that freedom as a launchpad for self-indulgence; instead, serve one another through love.
The entire law is summed up in a single line: love your neighbor as yourself.
But if you're biting and devouring each other, watch out, or you'll end up destroying one another.
Here's what I mean: walk by the Spirit, and you won't carry out what the flesh craves.
The flesh wants what's against the Spirit, and the Spirit wants what's against the flesh — they're opposed to each other, so you don't do whatever you please.
But if the Spirit is leading you, you're not under the law.
The flesh's works are plain to see: sexual sin, moral filth, unrestrained indulgence,
idol worship, dabbling in magic, hostility, quarreling, jealousy, outbursts of rage, selfish ambition, factions, splits,
envy, drunkenness, wild parties, and things like these. I warn you, as I warned before: those who live this way won't inherit God's kingdom.
But the Spirit's fruit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
gentleness, and self-control. No law stands against things like these.
Those who belong to Christ Jesus have nailed the flesh, with its passions and cravings, to the cross.
Since we live by the Spirit, let's also stay in step with the Spirit.
Let's not become conceited, provoking one another, or envying each other.
